- If sentiment is positive (≥0.2) and forecast is rising sharply, reduce forecast slope to avoid over-optimism.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.0) and forecast is rising, cap upward movement to prevent false bullishness.  
- If recent history shows strong upward momentum (e.g., 3+ consecutive spikes) and forecast continues rising linearly, introduce mean reversion bias after 5–7 days.  
- If true outcome shows sharp drop after a peak, reduce forecast slope by 10–20% for next 3–5 days to account for momentum decay.  
- If forecast is flat or slightly rising but true outcome shows strong divergence (e.g., >5% deviation from 30d mean), adjust downward by 2–5% for next 5 days if sentiment is neutral or negative.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.2 spikes with no true breakout, treat as “false signal” and reduce forecast amplitude by 5–10% for next 7 days.
